title: Why do you need health insurance for senior citizens?
content: Health insurance is a necessity for everyone, and it's particularly important for older people. Even if they're in good health, circumstances can change as the years pass. Therefore, having a health insurance plan for unexpected events is wise. It's worth noting that many health insurance plans come with waiting periods, so obtaining coverage as early as possible is advisable. You can navigate the waiting period and proactively manage potential risks.

title: Waiting Periods
content: 1. Pre-existing disease waiting period of 36 months since inception of the policy and continuous renewal 2. Initial waiting period of 30 days unless the treatment needed is the result of an accident 3. Specific waiting period of 24 months for some listed illnesses, unless the condition is directly caused by cancer (covered after initial waiting period of 30 days) or an accident (covered from day 1) Please note that Waiting Periods shall not apply to e-consultation, Personal Accident Cover and Critical Illness Cover. Please do read more about the common exclusions in the policy terms & conditions with title Waiting Period

title: Key Features of 1 Crore Health Insurance
content:
High Sum Insured -- Description: Covers medical expenses up to INR 1 crore, including hospitalisation and surgeries.
Cashless Hospitalisation -- Description: Access to a wide network of hospitals for cashless treatment.
Pre- and Post-Hospitalisation -- Description: Covers expenses 60–90 days before and after hospitalisation.
Critical Illness Coverage -- Description: Includes treatment for life-threatening diseases like cancer or heart ailments.
No-Claim Bonus (NCB) -- Description: Increases sum insured or offers premium discounts for claim-free years.
Restoration Benefit -- Description: Replenishes the sum insured if exhausted during a policy year.
Tax Deductions -- Description: Premiums eligible for tax benefits under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act.
Global Coverage -- Description: Some plans cover planned or emergency treatments abroad.

title: Common Exclusions in 1 Crore Health Insurance Plans
content:
While health insurance for 1 crore offers extensive coverage, certain exclusions apply. Being aware of these can help you avoid claim rejections. Common exclusions include:
Pre-Existing Diseases: Covered after a waiting period (usually 2–4 years).Cosmetic Treatments: Procedures like plastic surgery are typically not covered.Self-Inflicted Injuries: Injuries due to suicide attempts or substance abuse are excluded.Non-Allopathic Treatments: Some plans may not cover Ayurveda, Unani, or homeopathy unless specified.Maternity Expenses: Coverage may be limited or excluded unless included as an add-on.
Always read the policy document carefully to understand the inclusions and exclusions of your 1 crore medical insurance plan.

title: Grace period for premium payment
content: Life insurance policies carry a grace period of 30 days from the premium due date. The policy stays in force during the grace period. If the premium is unpaid when the grace period ends, the policy lapses.
answer_text: May 30 days po kayong grace period from the due date. Active pa rin po ang policy ninyo within that period. Pag lumagpas po, saka lang mag-la-lapse.

title: Late payment penalty
content: A late fee is charged per day of delay on an overdue instalment, calculated as a percentage of the outstanding instalment amount. The exact rate is stated in the financing agreement.
